## Reproduce without a decoder

Linux, Python 3.12+, C compiler, make, pkg-config, patch, nm and libva development
headers are required for the real build. The model/extracted-function tests need a C
compiler. All inputs are public pinned source or synthetic structs; no media is needed.

```
python3 experiments/h264-client-selection/tests.py
python3 experiments/h264-client-selection/actual-gate-test.py
python3 experiments/h264-client-selection/build-reproduction.py /tmp/h264-rejected-build
```

Use a **fresh** destination. The last command builds the full unpatched minimal FFmpeg
client successfully, then requires the specific rejected-patch link failure, and finally
requires two additional compiler failures after enabling the missing glue section.
A dependency/baseline failure is an error, never accepted as a successful reproduction.
It writes commands, logs and `report.json` with source/archive/patch/compiler/config,
baseline executable and log identities. `build-evidence.json` records the maintainer's
Linux aarch64 run; CI also reproduces it on Ubuntu. No binary is run against VA or installed.

`prepare.py` retains the original five hash-locked source-file preparation for analysis.
It refuses by default; `--reproduce-rejected` explicitly selects the known-broken archive.
The manifest hashes all seven patched files, including both newly added files. The
`rejected/` patch and C/header preserve contributor head
`89c2371015ca342225038f1ead55463339d3f0e0` byte-for-byte. Their comments are historical
proposal claims, not accepted conclusions.

## Confirmed blockers

| Boundary | Reproducible finding | Consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Actual configured build | New C translation unit does not include `config_components.h` before `#if CONFIG_H264_VAAPI_HWACCEL`; object omits all five `ff_h264_vaapi_*` functions | Object-only and model checks pass, but real client link fails with five undefined references |
| Activating the omitted glue | Adding only the config include exposes `H264_NAL_SLICE` macro collision with FFmpeg's enum and incomplete `AVCodecInternal` accesses | The earlier missing-include finding was moved, not resolved |
| Actual `ff_h264_vaapi_gate_end` | Mechanically extracted function accepts a zeroed session with no picture or slice; an added `in_picture` check changes that result | The model's fail-closed end test does not cover the actual gate. This is admission, not a measured hardware submission |
| Backend ownership (source observation) | `h264dec.c` tests any `avctx->hwaccel` before calling a function that casts private data to `VAAPIDecodeContext` | With VAAPI compiled and another backend active, the proposed hook has the wrong owner; no non-VA runtime experiment was performed |
| Dispatch (source observation) | Pinned `decode_nal_units` ignores auxiliary NAL19 and extension/default NALs; patch changes only DPA/DPB/DPC and some errors | Unsupported syntax after an accepted prefix is not comprehensively canceled |
| Actual configuration (source observation) | Glue invents a CB/Main/High advertisement mask; helper-selected profile is not the VA config selected by `vaapi_decode.c` | High10 and profile changes do not retain the required device/config contract |

The end-gate reproduction compiles the **actual function text**, with minimal synthetic
storage definitions and no VA issue call. Its repair mutation must break the blocking
assertion. It is not a full parser/callback extraction. The original six test groups now
explicitly identify their C helper as a **standalone model**; compiling the same file while
its FFmpeg section is preprocessed out is insufficient evidence. The FMO mutation tests
that model only. `h264_va_on_nal` is handwritten dispatch, not `decode_nal_units`.

## Required implementation boundary

Follow-up #79 must build with VAAPI on/off, exercise the real parser/dispatch and issue/cancel
callbacks, and verify zero submissions for empty/rejected pictures and exactly one for
accepted pictures. Include a non-VA canary fixture, auxiliary/extension/partition NALs,
malformed later slices/SPS/PPS, actual configured profiles, and unchanged-ID parameter
replacement. Admission must validate every required feature before issue; if that cannot
be established, remapping stays disabled. An **explicit stop** is acceptable; seamless
software fallback additionally requires reference-state recovery/replay.

The accepted whole-inventory Python oracle in `experiments/h264-profile-selection/`
remains separate. Its synthetic feature flags are not measured vector inventories. Neither
model nor this blocking reproduction proves any of the five candidate vectors now plays
normally. Parent #37 retains real five-vector exact outputs, the 135-vector pass-set
comparison, recovery behavior and support documentation.
